title: Aggrega Infrastructure Base (FeatureRecipe)
description: Ops-authored definitions mapping Dev abstract features to concrete, versioned Go plugin pipelines. Strictly 1:1 with a physical provider and catalog feature.

version.description: Strict Semantic Versioning of the feature plugin pipeline (e.g., 1.2.5).

description.description: What this entity is and what it is for, written for someone deciding whether to use it. Open with a sentence naming the thing, then add what a reader needs in order to choose it and use it correctly — what it expects from a deployment, and anything surprising about how it behaves. A short paragraph is the usual length.

maintainers.description: List of maintainers who own this entity.

license.description: SPDX identifier for the license of the software this entity describes, such as MIT or AGPL-3.0. It records the terms of that software, not the terms of this file.

repository.description: The URL to the Git repository where the source files live.

home.description: The URL of this entity's home page, wiki, or documentation.

keywords.description: A list of descriptive keywords for UI discoverability.

spec.description: The provider capability binding, mapping, pipeline, and inject mapping for a FeatureRecipe. Carries the same three input kinds as a Recipe (sourced, synthesized, artifacts) plus the FeatureRecipe-only injectMapping; a pure-wiring FeatureRecipe declaring only capability and implements is valid and renders nothing.

capability.description: Selects the in-memory evaluation branch. It matches the capability by its bare name, so a declaration carrying a version pin ('eval:1.0.0', 'eval:^1.0.0') selects the same branch as the unpinned 'eval': the pin selects which plugin version serves the capability and is not part of the capability name. A longer name that merely begins with those letters, such as 'evaluate', is a different capability and does not select it.

then.description: The eval provider executes formatting in-memory. Fetching a 'source', a 'workload', or 'artifacts', or leaving what a source renders out with 'omits', is mathematically banned. injectMapping (a delivery transform, not a rendering surface) remains allowed.

else.description: Non-eval capabilities use the three-input-kinds model (sourced, synthesized, artifacts) plus the FeatureRecipe-only injectMapping. Unlike a Recipe, a FeatureRecipe is not required to declare any input kind: a pure-wiring FeatureRecipe (capability + implements only) is valid and renders nothing — its effect is the uses-edge the Feature it implements carries. Pairing rules apply: valuesMapping requires source; omits requires source; and a workload: block requires a provider that supports workload synthesis — a synthesized-mode FeatureRecipe bound to a non-synthesizing provider halts loudly at render time.

capability.description: The explicit provider capability this recipe binds to (e.g., 'helm', 'terraform', 'compose') — the provider kind that renders it.

implements.description: Declares which catalog Feature type this recipe is able to implement (including credential Features labeled feature.aggrega.ai/kind: secret; exact version, major-compatible range '^', or unversioned). The compiler uses it to verify Manifest mappings and to suggest candidates in diagnostics and editor completion; it never resolves a build. The Manifest mapping is the user's explicit deployment choice, pinned in the lockfile.

locals.description: The Private Ops State. Internal computation results available only within this FeatureRecipe's templates as '.locals.*'. Each entry is itself a Go template, evaluated against a self-contained context: '.context.instance_id' (the HOST COMPONENT this attachment is resolving for, which is what that reference denotes on every template surface), '.attachment_name' (the attachment instance being resolved, and the only route to that name from a local), the attachment's own '.values' and '.infra', and the entries of this same block resolved so far. Entries resolve in the order they are written, and an entry MAY read a sibling defined ABOVE it, receiving that sibling's resolved value rather than its template text. Author order is part of the contract wherever one entry reads another: moving a definition below its reader breaks the build, and the block is never reordered to make a reference resolve. A '.locals.<key>' reference to an entry this block defines LATER halts naming the ordering fault; one naming a key the block does not declare at all halts naming the key. Both checks read the path a reference RESOLVES to rather than the keystrokes, so they cover the direct form, a read inside a '{{ with .locals }}' block, and a read through a variable bound directly to '.locals' alike. Two spellings they do not cover. One is a reference whose path the template text does not decide — one reached through a function, such as 'index .locals', or through a 'with' block or a variable binding whose pipeline applies one, since what such a pipeline yields is decided at evaluation rather than by its text. The other is a key read off a parenthesised block, '(.locals).<key>' or '($.locals).<key>', where the key hangs off the value the parentheses yield rather than off the block itself. Neither is analysed, and an absent key reached either way does not halt: it renders the literal text '<no value>' rather than nothing at all. The one exception is 'index' itself: on every template surface it halts, naming the key, when the map it reads does not hold the key it is asked for, so an absent key reached through 'index .locals' halts. This FeatureRecipe's locals resolve BEFORE its provides, so a provides template may read '.locals' and receives resolved values, while a provides template naming a key this block does not declare halts. The rules are the same ones a Recipe's locals block follows. Used to export physical realities (e.g., target containers, JSON paths) for downstream Wasm plugins. Never exposed to callers — use provides for the public API.

provides.description: The Public Developer API. Contractual output variables available for downstream Caller inject resolution.

source.description: Optional path to infrastructure code. Accepts a Universal URI string or an open structured object. If provided alongside valuesMapping, the compiler renders it and appends the objects to the base AST before Wasm plugins execute.

oneOf.description: Universal URI string (e.g., './src', 'git::https://...', 'oci://...'). Used for local paths, OCI artifacts, and Git repositories.
Open Structured Object. The exact required keys (e.g., 'registry', 'chart' for Helm) are dictated and validated dynamically at compile-time by the Provider's Wasm socket.

valuesMapping.description: Values mapping content with three authoring modes via content-shape dispatch. Mode 1 (inline): a Go template string scalar producing the provider's expected values format. Mode 2 (file import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: ./relative/path.tmpl`, pointing at a local Go-template file. Mode 3 (library import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: <Library>#/mappings/<entry>`, referencing a MappingLibrary entry by bare-name identity (the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile; no registry host appears in the reference).

$import.description: A local file path, or a bare-name MappingLibrary reference `<Library>#/mappings/<entry>`. A registry host (`oci://…`) is rejected: a library is addressed by identity, and the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile.

workload.description: Workload YAML producer with three authoring modes via content-shape dispatch. Mode 1 (inline): a Go template string scalar whose output parses as 'aggrega.ai/v1alpha1 Workload'. Mode 2 (file import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: ./relative/path.yaml`, pointing at a local Go-template file. Mode 3 (library import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: <Library>#/workloads/<entry>`, referencing a WorkloadLibrary entry by bare-name identity (the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile; no registry host appears in the reference). The target Provider must support workload synthesis; the standard-library catalog declares workloadSchema on such providers as the documented contract. A workload: FeatureRecipe bound to a provider that cannot synthesize halts loudly at render time. A synthesized FeatureRecipe workload emits its provider-native manifests under the feature's output directory.

$import.description: A local file path, or a bare-name WorkloadLibrary reference `<Library>#/workloads/<entry>`. A registry host (`oci://…`) is rejected: a library is addressed by identity, and the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile.

artifacts.description: Map of entry name to artifact-content authoring. Each entry's value carries one of three modes via content-shape dispatch. Mode 1 (inline): a Go template string scalar whose output is the artifact body. Mode 2 (file import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: ./relative/path.yaml`, pointing at a local Go-template file. Mode 3 (library import): a YAML map of exactly one key, `$import: <Library>#/artifacts/<entry>`, referencing an ArtifactLibrary bundle by bare-name identity (the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile; no registry host appears in the reference). A bundle expands into one output per file, each nested under the entry's key as `<key>/<filename>`. The key names the entry's output: a mode-1 or mode-2 entry's key is its output filename, used as written, and a mode-2 entry's imported file supplies the content without naming the output, so two entries importing different files that share a name are two distinct outputs. The auxiliary resources a resource-generating FeatureRecipe emits (ConfigMap, ServiceMonitor, NetworkPolicy, ExternalSecret CRD, etc.) are artifact-shaped; artifacts: is the primary resource-generation mechanism. Collisions across artifact entries, bundle files, source output, and workload synthesis halt the build when the node renders. The `artifacts` block is authored identically on a Recipe and on a FeatureRecipe — the same three modes, the same key-to-output rule and the same collision behaviour — which is why that part of this description reads the same on both kinds; an example written for one transfers to the other unchanged.

propertyNames.description: The key names the entry's output, so it is bounded to a single filename: it begins with a letter or digit and continues with letters, digits, dots, hyphens or underscores. Dots after the first character keep the extensions artifact keys carry (`main.tf`, `template.yaml`, `serviceaccount.yaml`). A `/` would make one key name a path rather than a file, and a leading `.` would admit `..`, which names a location outside the output directory — the first character class refuses both. For a library import the key names the directory the bundle's files are nested under, so the same bound applies.

$import.description: A local file path, or a bare-name ArtifactLibrary reference `<Library>#/artifacts/<entry>` (the entry names a bundle). A registry host (`oci://…`) is rejected: a library is addressed by identity, and the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile.

omits.description: What to leave out of what this FeatureRecipe's source renders — for a source taken as it is that renders something the Release must not ship: a document a fetched chart renders, such as a Secret holding a key the chart generates afresh on every render, a service, a volume or a config a fetched compose file bundles, or a resource a fetched CloudFormation template declares. Most FeatureRecipes never need it. Each entry names one unit the source renders by its kind, its name and, where the entry gives one, its namespace, each in the vocabulary of the provider rendering the source — for a chart, a document by its own `kind` and `metadata.name`; for a compose file, a `service`, a `volume` or a `config` by its key under `services:`, `volumes:` or `configs:`; for a CloudFormation template, a resource by its `Type` and its logical ID. That provider leaves out every unit an entry matches, and what an entry matches, and what the provider refuses on an entry's account, is that provider's own documented contract. A provider that cannot leave anything out refuses a FeatureRecipe declaring this key before anything is rendered. Only what `source:` renders is filtered — a `workload:` or an `artifacts:` entry never is — so the key requires `source` and is refused on an `eval` FeatureRecipe. Every value is a template, evaluated against the context `valuesMapping` is evaluated against. An entry's `when` is evaluated first, and an entry whose `when` renders a falsy value is dropped. Every entry left active must leave something out: an active entry that matches nothing the source rendered halts the build, naming the entry. The source still renders in full — every template of a chart still runs, so a template that fails still fails the build — and only its output is left out. The key is authored identically on a Recipe and on a FeatureRecipe.

kind.description: The kind of the unit to leave out, in the vocabulary of the provider rendering the source: for a chart, a rendered document's own `kind`, such as `Secret`; for a compose file, `service`, `volume` or `config`; for a CloudFormation template, a resource's `Type`, such as `AWS::S3::Bucket`. It names a kind the source renders, and is unrelated to the `kind:` a structured `source:` carries. A template.

name.description: The name of the unit to leave out, in the vocabulary of the provider rendering the source: for a chart, a rendered document's own `metadata.name`; for a compose file, the unit's key under `services:`, `volumes:` or `configs:`; for a CloudFormation template, the resource's logical ID, its key under `Resources`. A template.

namespace.description: The namespace the unit to leave out is in, when the entry should match only a unit in that namespace — for a provider whose output has namespaces, as a chart's rendered documents do. Absent, or rendering to the empty string, the entry matches a unit of its kind and name whatever its namespace. A compose file and a CloudFormation template have no namespaces, and their providers refuse an entry that names one. A template.

when.description: Inline Go template evaluated before the entry's other fields. When it renders a falsy value the entry is dropped: its other fields are not evaluated, nothing is left out on its account, and it is not required to match. An empty or absent `when` keeps the entry. Truthiness follows the standard convention for boolean-like template output: the strings `true`/`True`/`TRUE`, any nonzero number, and any other non-empty string are true, while `false`/`False`/`FALSE`, the empty string, and zero are false. A `when` that fails to render halts the build.

injectMapping.description: Optional inline Go template evaluated during the Pre-Render Interception phase. Outputs a JSON/YAML dictionary that the Go compiler natively deep-merges over the Caller's '.context.inject' memory pipe. Used for Wasm-free Caller-Side mutation of environment variables and delivery contracts.

pipeline.description: Sequential list of Wasm plugins to execute for stateful AST mutation.

id.description: A unique programmatic identifier for this step, allowing downstream plugins to reference its outputs.

plugin.description: The reference to the Plugin entity this step runs, always scoped by the plugin's own socket type: `<pluginType>/<name>` with an optional version, as in `parser/yaml` or `parser/yaml:1.0.0`. The scope is mandatory rather than one form among several — an unscoped `name:version` is refused, because two sockets may hold a plugin of the same name and the scope is what makes the entity resolvable. The entity's spec.plugin is the content-addressed .wasm artifact; the build resolves the entity to its artifact and loads the bytes. A bare .wasm or artifact reference is not accepted here.

function.description: The exported Wasm function to invoke.

with.description: Inline Go template evaluating to a JSON/YAML map that strictly satisfies this plugin's explicit input schema.

optional.description: When true, a failure of this step (a guest trap, a patch targeting a document not present in the set, a malformed patch, or a halt-severity diagnostic) is downgraded to a loud warning: the pre-step document set is restored, this step's output is discarded, and the pipeline continues. When false or absent, any step failure halts the build after restoring the pre-step document set.

when.description: Inline Go template evaluated at pipeline-walk time. When it renders a falsy value the step is skipped — a pass-through: the document set flows to the next step unchanged, contributing no patches, side effects, or step record. An empty or absent `when` always runs the step. Truthiness follows the standard convention for boolean-like template output: the strings `true`/`True`/`TRUE`, any nonzero number, and any other non-empty string are true, while `false`/`False`/`FALSE`, the empty string, and zero are false. `when` and `optional` are independent: a step may declare both.

executionScope.description: Whether this FeatureRecipe's Resource Generation runs per-component (default, today's behavior) or once per boundary attachment. Boundary-scope FeatureRecipes deduplicate by (boundary_path, FR-instance) and receive a different TemplateContext shape (.boundary.* pillars instead of per-component .context.* pillars). The injectMapping continues to fan per-consumer regardless of executionScope.

readsCallerRenderFacts.description: Declares that this FeatureRecipe's templates read what the Components connecting to the one it is attached to rendered: the render facts each of those callers' providers reports about its own output. Where it is true and the FeatureRecipe renders per component, each attachment of it renders after every Component in the build has rendered, instead of right after the Component it is attached to, so each caller's render is complete before the attachment is evaluated. Where it is false or absent, the attachment renders right after its Component, and the build halts on a template written inline in this FeatureRecipe that reads a caller's render facts beneath '.context.used_by'.

assertions.description: Build-time cross-field validation. Each entry is a named assertion: the key is a stable rule identifier surfaced in error messages; the value is a Go template string with `{{ fail "message" }}` halt semantics. Multiple named assertions per entity evaluate per-instance in author-declared order; the first failing assertion halts the build. FeatureRecipe assertions evaluate after recipe binding (post-binding, post-allProvides-evaluation, pre-render) and express implementation invariants of the specific chart or module the FeatureRecipe sources. Template context: .values / .infra / .uses / .features / .metadata plus .provides / .locals / .recipe. The evaluator uses missingkey=error: references to undefined keys halt with a no-such-key diagnostic. Because the bare reference halts before any fallback can run, a plain `default` does not supply an optional-field fallback on this surface — gate the reference with `hasKey`, or use the `optional` helper, which performs the presence check directly. Reading the key through `index` does not supply one either: `index` halts on a map key the map does not hold, naming the key.
